subject: Trial traffic ingest, success criteria & rollout map — BrightCart POC
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moroz <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12 15:02 PDT
Subject: Post-call recap + traffic intake (BrightCart POC)

Hi Elena — great to meet you and the BrightCart platform team today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we have a single source of truth going into the POC: 

1) Trial objective & success criteria (proposed)
- Objective: validate Redwood inference for BrightCart checkout-assist feature under representative traffic and verify latency/cost goals.
- Success: P95 inference latency <= 350ms for combined prompt+response up to 512 tokens; <1% error/timeout rate; 2% or lower cost per session compared to your current baseline.

2) Evaluation plan / timeline (proposed)
- Intake & sample data collection: by 7/16
- Dry-run smoke test on staging: 7/18
- POC window (live-like load): 7/21–8/03 (2 weeks)
- Final review & decision: week of 8/10

3) Workload / traffic profile we discussed — please confirm these values or paste your real traffic into the attached template (traffic-intake-template.xlsx):
- Average steady-state RPS: 8–12 RPS
- Peak burst RPS: up to 140 RPS for short windows (1–3 minutes) during US lunch and major sale events
- Typical session pattern: 3–4 calls per user session
- Typical prompt token length (user message): mean ~45 tokens, 95th pct <= 120 tokens
- Typical response token length (model output): mean ~180 tokens, 95th pct <= 420 tokens
- Concurrency target: 35–60 concurrent sessions in high-traffic windows
- KV/cache usage: per-session context reused 80% of the time (benefits from prefix cache)

4) Ownership
- Redwood: onboarding, model serving config, infra monitoring, cost telemetry (Jonas, Rishi)
- BrightCart: provide sample anonymized traffic, test account, success metrics baseline (Elena)

5) Immediate asks from us
- Please fill the attached traffic template with one week of anonymized request metadata (timestamps, token counts, success/failure flags) by 7/16.
- Confirm whether any PII must be redacted beyond standard anonymization.

I'll stand up a short Slack channel after you confirm for quicker coordination. Attaching the traffic template and a minimal poc-config.json with our initial ingestion fields.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: traffic-intake-template.xlsx (xlsx)
Attachments: poc-config.json (json)
From: Elena Moroz <elena@brightcart.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart Platform Team <platform@brightcart.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-13 09:41 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + traffic intake (BrightCart POC)

Jonas — thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our side after a quick sync with the platform team: 

- The steady-state RPS you have is about right for our normal days; during promotions our bursts can hit ~180 RPS for 60–90s (we said 140 on the call as a conservative number). Can you handle that headroom?
- Prompt/response tokens: our current data shows user prompts avg ~30 tokens (we're aggressively truncating) and model responses avg ~140 tokens. The 95th pct numbers you suggested are fine.
- Concurrency: our checkout funnel keeps sessions pinned; you can expect spikes up to 120 concurrent sessions for 2–3 mins during major events.
- We will provide a privacy-scrubbed export by 7/15. Will include request timestamp, prompt token count, response token count, and a flag whether the session hit a cached prefix.

One operational question: what model variants will Redwood try during the POC? Are you planning to test multiple quantization profiles (8-bit vs 4-bit) or keep it to a single configuration? We want to understand likely cost delta up front.

Elena Moroz
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightCart
elena@brightcart.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Elena Moroz <elena@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-07-13 11:15 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + traffic intake (BrightCart POC)

Hi all — quick technical follow-up and what we'll validate on the infra side. Thanks for the numbers, Elena — good to have the tighter burst/conc concurrency values. Notes: 

Planned config during POC
- Default model: redwood/llm-3-medium (fp16) for baseline latency; fallbacks: redwood/llm-3-small-quant (4-bit) for cost experiments
- Autoscaling window: aggressive ramp for burst tolerance (scale target within 60s for short spikes)
- KV caching: enable per-session prefix cache; we will instrument cache hit rate in telemetry

Acceptance criteria (technical)
- P95 end-to-end inference latency <= 350ms for combined prompt+response when response <= 512 tokens (measured at our edge in us-west)
- Error rate (5xx/timeouts) <= 1% across POC window
- Cache hit rate >= 45% for repeated sessions (if BrightCart traffic shows repeat contexts)
- Cost measurement: tokens-per-dollar baseline vs quantized run; target <2.5x the cheapest quantized option when meeting latency SLOs

What we need from BrightCart to run the dry-run (by 7/16)
- One-week anonymized traces in the template format (timestamps, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, cached_flag)
- A representative sample of typical prompt templates (5–10 examples) so we can build prompt-based caching keys
- Contact for infra escalation (pager/email) — we assume Elena for now

I'll prepare a minimal poc-config.json with the autoscale and model-fallback entries and share it in the channel. If these acceptance criteria look good, we'll lock the trial start for 7/21 and plan two measurement checkpoints (end of week 1 and end of week 2).

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moroz <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, BrightCart Platform Team <platform@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-07-14 08:27 PDT
Subject: Re: Trial traffic ingest, success criteria & rollout map — BrightCart POC

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Finalizing next steps below and closing the loop on ownership/timelines: 

Confirmed timeline
- BrightCart provides anonymized template: due 7/15 (Elena) — NOTE: earlier in thread we said 7/16; please confirm if 7/15 is impossible and we'll accept 7/16.
- Dry-run staging smoke: 7/18 (Redwood infra lead: Rishi)
- POC window: 7/21–8/03 (analytics checkpoints 7/28 and 8/03)

Finalized success criteria (agreed)
- Business: measurable reduction in latency for checkout flows and acceptable cost delta vs baseline (BrightCart to provide baseline cost metric)
- Technical: P95 <= 350ms for <=512 tokens, <=1% error rate, cache hit target >=45%

Immediate items for signatures / procurement
- I'll send the DocuSign MSA (link below) for the POC engagement; sign/return to enable reserved trial capacity.

Action owners
- BrightCart: provide template + anonymization confirmation (Elena)
- Redwood: prepare poc-config + staging runbook (Rishi), report dashboards (Lauren)
- Sales: finalize trial SOW & confirm billing hold (Jonas)

Related references
- HubSpot deal: HS-34521
- DocuSign MSA: https://www.docusign.com/BC-MSA-34521
- Drive folder with config & dashboards: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxx/brightcart-poc

If you confirm the delivery dates for the template and the MSA signature ETA, we'll lock the kickoff for 7/21. I'll open a short Slack channel for day-to-day coordination once the MSA is signed.

Thanks — excited to get this running.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0189
